findings.text: Releases one reference on a per address space private futex table. A null argument is accepted and ignored. When the release reports the final reference, waiters sleeping on the owning address space descriptor are awakened so a pending table replacement can proceed.

Reference release operates in two modes selected by table state. In per CPU mode the current CPU counter is decremented and final release is never reported. In shared mode a process wide atomic counter is decremented and final release is reported exactly when it reaches zero. Preemption remains disabled across the state observation and the decrement.

Privacy of a key is determined solely by absence of both shared kind markers in its offset component. Key construction is trusted to set at least one marker for every shared key, so unmarked keys can be treated as process private without further checks.

Table migration preserves waiter membership while moving every waiter from each old bucket to its new bucket. Each old bucket lock is held while its chain is drained, population counts are adjusted on removal and arrival, each waiter is expected to still point at the old bucket lock, and each destination lock is taken with a nesting annotation before linking and updating the waiter back pointer.

Bucket selection prefers a private table when no explicit node is requested, the key tests private, and a usable private table is visible with an optional output reference to the caller. Otherwise a global hash over key identity and offset selects a bucket. When no node is specified the same hash also spreads buckets across possible nodes with wrap around to the next possible node.

On multiprocessor builds each bucket carries a population count raised on waiter arrival and lowered on departure, with a full barrier after the increment to order against wake side observation. Uniprocessor builds omit the counter entirely.

Private table replacement cycles through absent, published per CPU, draining shared, pending replacement and retired states. A replacement can only be published when no table exists or the current table has no remaining shared references; otherwise it waits as pending. Publication marks the new table per CPU, publishes with ordering, records a later grace epoch for reference drops, and retires the old table asynchronously. Lookup paths that fail to acquire a reference drive the pivot and retry.

Bucket resolution exists in full and minimal configurations. The full form returns a bucket paired with an optionally referenced private table under read side protection and retries through a pivot when the private table cannot be referenced. The minimal form returns only the bucket with no private table handling.

Node attribution prefers a validated caller supplied node, then a memory policy derived node from preferred or bound policies with home node handling, and finally either the local node or hash based interleaving when nothing else applies. Policy lookup first tries a speculative read that may report busy or stale, falling back to a sleeping read lock; a minimal build always reports absence of node.

Key construction enforces natural alignment from size flags with doubled transfer for NUMA variants, checks user accessibility and fault injection, resolves and optionally writes back NUMA node information, and records the node in the key. Private keys finish quickly by pairing the current address space with the aligned address without page lookup. Shared keys pin the backing page with write preference and read fallback for read waiters, then form either an address space based key for anonymous memory or an inode sequence plus file offset key for file memory, retrying on mapping instability and rejecting unusable or read only anonymous pages.

Each inode receives at most one nonzero sequence number allocated monotonically from a global counter. The first observer installs the value with compare exchange while losers adopt the winning value. A zero allocation is discarded with a warning and retried to preserve the nonzero invariant.

Deadline preparation returns absence when no time is supplied. Otherwise it initializes a stack resident sleeper in absolute mode using real time or monotonic clock according to flags and programs the deadline together with the caller supplied slack range.

Write fault preparation serializes with the address space read lock while requesting a write fault fixup for the target user address, then releases the lock and normalizes the outcome to success or the underlying fault error.

Wake selection scans a single bucket chain in priority order and returns the first waiter whose key matches the target, or absence when none matches. Key equality requires both keys present with identical word, pointer and offset components.

Ownership handoff waiting acts only when the prior operation reported busy together with an exiting owner task. It briefly holds the exiting task exit mutex to serialize against teardown, then releases its task reference. Other statuses or a missing owner are treated as warning cases with no wait.

A futex key combines page offset plus kind markers, a node selector, and either a private address space plus address pair or a shared inode sequence plus file offset pair, with aliased storage for the identity fields used during matching. A bucket reference pairs a bucket pointer with an optional private table reference. A private table links its owning address space, a lifetime state, a mask sizing its bucket array, and reference storage in per CPU or shared atomic form.

Transfer size is a power of two selected by masked flag bits, doubled when NUMA handling is requested. Page offset shares its field with dedicated markers that distinguish inode based and shared address space keys from private keys. A dedicated sentinel value denotes absence of an explicit node choice.
Standard mutex acquisition may sleep. It first attempts a fast atomic acquisition and enters the sleeping slow path only when that attempt fails.

Fast mutex acquisition first checks internal consistency through a build dependent warning helper, then attempts to move ownership from unowned to current with acquire ordering. Success alone grants the lock with no further synchronization.

Mutex slow acquisition progresses from fast retry and optimistic spinning to queued sleep with possible direct handoff. Ordinary waiters queue in FIFO order while wound wait transactions queue in timestamp order with early kill and wound handling. Sleepers use the requested sleep state, recheck ownership after each wake, abort on pending signals, allow the queue head extra optimistic spinning with temporary lock release, and accept handoff from the releaser. Success detaches the waiter and records acquisition while failure detaches, releases dependency state and returns the terminal status.

The mutex slow path disables preemption for its whole duration, guards queue and ownership changes with an interrupt saving spin lock, and separately guards task blocking state with the task blocked lock that records the blocking object across sleeps. Dependency and contention tracking spans from entry until success or cancellation, with deferred wakes flushed when the queue lock is released.

Wound wait mutex use introduces extra failure modes. Reacquiring a context already held fails immediately, wound state is cleared when a fresh transaction starts, and a waiter may be forced to abort when a conflicting transaction wounds it, including after stealing ownership out of queue order.

Table migration and replacement expose two races. A waiter already moved to a not yet published new table may concurrently depart through timeout or signal, so removal must tolerate unpublished membership. A second replacement must not overwrite an already pending table, and grace tracking must begin only after publication to avoid early reclamation.
Mutex consistency warnings have two mutually exclusive build forms. Debug builds emit a lock debug warning on violation while non debug builds compile the check away entirely.
